title: The Raven's Legacy
description: The Great Treasure is within reach...

mainQuestExcel.title: The Raven's Legacy
mainQuestExcel.description: The Great Treasure is within reach...

flow.stepDescription: Go to Piramida to look for clues

dialogs.text: Tolfin! What are you doing here?
Ah, fantastic, just the duo I was waiting for.
Huh? How did you know we would come here? H—Have you been following us since we parted at Blue Amber Lake!?
Haha! I was only joking. I came back to visit my parents and just so happened to be running errands here in Piramida when I spotted the two of you.
Paimon sees... Huh? So you have family here?
What's strange about that? Just like a raven is born to raven parents, people don't magically appear out of thin air.
That's not what Paimon meant! Hmm... Though come to think of it, we're not really that close, and Paimon can see how it was kind of a personal question...
Can I ask a question that isn't so personal?
Good idea! Tolfin knows everyone and everything — he just might have the info we need.
You recount your experiences searching for, and finding, the Proofs of the Cognoscenti after leaving Blue Amber Lake...
So Tolfin, do you have any idea where the last Proof of the Cognoscenti might be?
I do have a few thoughts, however...
#Hmm, seeing as it's {NICKNAME}, {M#he}{F#she}'ll probably be fine. From everything I've heard about your adventures, I believe {M#he}{F#she} should be able to overcome the trial.
There's another trial? ...It isn't going to be impossible, is it?
#Of course not. Besides, I have total confidence in your abilities, {NICKNAME}.
Ahem, the last Proof of the Cognoscenti is actually with my grandmother. I'm on my way to visit her now — why don't you tag along?
#Seriously?! What are the chances? Tolfin's grandmother... What do you think she's like, {NICKNAME}? Do you think she's the kind of sweet old lady who loves to tell stories?
She does tell stories, but... Never mind, you'll see when we get there.
Then why didn't you tell us about it back at Blue Amber Lake...?
Mmm... Well, the fact we can meet here again is a sign that our fates are somehow intertwined. Rather than dwell on the past, we should look toward the future instead...
Wow. That change of subject couldn't have felt any more forced if you'd tried!

flow.stepDescription: Go to the place indicated by Tolfin

dialogs.text: Well, well, well, look who's remembered to visit! Did you take care of that matter for me, you little brat?
Of course I did! Would I dare show my face here if I hadn't?
Ahem... This is my grandmother. Though I'm sure she'd rather be known as "Hiljetta, the Black-Barrel Hag" than "a failed merchant's grandmother."
She doesn't seem too friendly...
She doesn't look anything like Tolfin at all... She's far too serious...
I hear that a lot. But at the end of the day, we're family, and we're a lot more alike than people think.
#This is {NICKNAME}, and this is Paimon. They've already found the other Proofs of the Cognoscenti...
Oh? So you've already found the other four? Well, that takes some real talent. But I'm afraid you're going to have to let me see that talent for myself.
Seeing as the brat brought you in, I won't make things too hard for you — how about we just trade a few moves?
Hold on a second! This... uhm... Something about this doesn't feel right...
And what exactly is the problem? If you want to get your hands on the Great Treasure, you'll naturally need to get past me first.
#She's a stubborn old bag of bones, but once she sees what you can do, everything'll be on the table. Come on, {NICKNAME}, it's in your hands now.
You don't look much like Tolfin.

flow.stepDescription: Have a friendly spar with the Black-Barrel Hag
Talk to Hiljetta

dialogs.text: Not bad, not bad at all! You do have promise. Here, this is the Proof of the Cognoscenti you've been seeking. But if you want to claim the Great Treasure, there's still one final path you'll have to tread.
#Not that it'll hold {M#him}{F#her} back — not considering how sharp the little {M#lad}{F#lass} is. {M#He}{F#She}'s a far more fitting heir to the Treasure Hoarders than you are, ya useless lump.
Heir to the Treasure Hoarders? Me?
Huh? So Granny is a Treasure Hoarder? And Tolfin, you too?
I guess you could say that.
#Paimon never would've guessed. You don't look like a Treasure Hoarder. Don't tell Paimon you knew about this all along, {NICKNAME}?
I figured it out pretty quickly...

...Don't tell me you didn't explain it to them? Were you really planning to deliver the Great Treasure to a couple of know-nothings who couldn't tell a Treasure Hoarder if they introduced themselves and brought them to their grandmother?
They've shown they have what it takes to gather the Proofs of the Cognoscenti — and they handled your challenge just fine. In fact, weren't you praising them just now?
You little...

#Alright, alright, don't give yourself a heart attack... I'll explain everything to them right now. I'll see to it that {NICKNAME} is willing to be the Treasure Hoarders' heir — exactly as you wanted!
Hmph! And you really think you can make all of that clear to them lickety-split?
What are you so worried about? You won't shut up about how I'm just like that "good-for-nothing Brahe." At least I inherited his gift for smooth talking, didn't I?
Tolfin leads you to a quiet corner to talk...
So what's really going on here? All we heard is that if we collect all five Proofs of the Cognoscenti, we can find the Great Treasure hidden "East of the Moon, West of the Sun"...
Are you seriously telling Paimon that we'd have to take over as leaders of the Treasure Hoarders just to get Reed Miller's treasure? Honestly, all this heir talk is weirding Paimon out...
It's hard to imagine anyone leading the Treasure Hoarders...
Exactly — there are people who call themselves Treasure Hoarders in every corner of Teyvat these days. And that's where the problem lies.
While we might be able to face reality, my stubborn old grandmother still dreams of a day when the Treasure Hoarders can restore their glory from the days of Reed Miller.
She fantasizes that someone will come along and rally the masses — "Let the dead bury the dead, and rise to build an Elysium for the hungry and the poor on the wealth of the high and haughty."
While most of us have heard how Reed Miller stole from the rich to help the poor, very few know that the Treasure Hoarders once defended Elysium from the dark abyss...
It was the Treasure Hoarders' golden age — it was the worst of times, and yet somehow it was also the best.
I don't know, maybe things are still the same today. But that era has passed, and she'll have to accept that someday.
You're not wrong... but what are we supposed to do about it?
#Before we go any further, {NICKNAME}, are you willing to serve as heir to the Treasure Hoarders and see that Reed Miller's dream is one day fulfilled?
I have my own dreams to fulfill...
Haha, just as I thought. Then how about we do it this way... Let's put on a little show!
Again!?
That's what you said back at Blue Amber Lake. Sure, you helped us get the Proof of the Cognoscenti back then... but who knows when you'll use those same sneaky tricks on us!
Why would I do anything to thwart you when we're already such good friends? Now, instead of being suspicious, how about we focus on what we're going to say.

You have a brief discussion with Tolfin about how to convince Hiljetta...\nAccording to Tolfin, simply mentioning the name "Avrelian" should be enough to gain her trust, and if she ever brings up the name "Brahe," all you have to say is that you don't agree with his methods.\nAs for who these two people actually are, Tolfin says it's a long story and promises to explain everything in detail when he gets the chance...
#So, what do you say, little {M#lad}{F#lass}? Are you in?
I will fulfill Avrelian's dream.
Good! That's the spirit. If it weren't for the little brat acting just like that good-for-nothing Brahe, the Proof of the Cognoscenti wouldn't have been scattered and lost for so long.
We're nothing like Tolfin... or that Brahe-ma-call-it fellow! You can rest assured!
#*sigh* Even I have to admit that {NICKNAME} is the most suitable candidate to inherit the Great Treasure.

Then it's settled, all that's left is for you to retrieve the Great Treasure. At the treasure site, you'll likely run into a few tricks left behind by that good-for-nothing... Hmph! I'm sure you'll be able to handle anything he came up with.
*sigh* Paimon still has no idea where "East of the Moon, West of the Sun" could be...
Oh, that... Well, it's beyond the horizon, yet so close you can touch it. Also, I won't be joining you for the next trial, so here's wishing you all the best!
Still, I'll be in Piramida for a little while longer, so please let me know if everything goes well. I'm counting on the both of you.
I just want to inherit the treasure he left behind...
I swear I had no idea...

flow.stepDescription: Go "East of the Moon, West of the Sun"

dialogs.text: Hurry — retrieve the Great Treasure.

dialogs.text: Look, it mentions Brahe over here. Looks like he was the one who made these records.
So Iron Coins were really the currency here back in the day... That means a mountain of these things could truly be called a "Great Treasure."
Ugh, if only we'd come here a few hundred years ago, we'd be rich! But Iron Coins aren't worth much Mora these days...
As they say, value lies in scarcity...
Exactly. So if we can find this... Prototype Iron Coin he wrote about, collectors are sure to go crazy for it! Paimon bets we could get a pretty penny for that one!
Too bad we don't know where it's buried. Ugh... Are we really supposed to dig up this whole place by ourselves?
We'll get a dressing down from the Black-Barrel Hag if we don't.
Oh yeah... you're right. We mustn't get on the wrong side of her. You might be able to handle her attacks, but Paimon will have to fly far, far away!
And speaking of the Black-Barrel Hag... now that Paimon has seen Brahe's notes and all these Iron Coins, she finally understands why that old lady wants to bring back the good old days.
To her, those days must have been the real Elysium.
Paimon thinks we're living in a pretty wonderful time, too! You and Paimon, and all the friends we've met on our journey... This is our golden age!
That's probably how Tolfin feels as well. He chose not to share the full history of the Treasure Hoarders with us because he didn't want us to bear the weight of expectation...

*sigh* It looks like this adventure ends here. Getting all five Proofs of the Cognoscenti wasn't easy, and Paimon knows it was far from a fruitless journey, but she can't help feeling a little disappointed.
By the way... Why do you think this ship is here?
Perhaps it sank under the weight of a greed it could not bear...

It would be risky to sail with all those heavy coins on board... Even if they didn't sink, they might get robbed! Oh, but this is a Treasure Hoarder ship — they're not usually the ones who would need to be scared.
That's such a shame. Even though this ship is hundreds of years old, it still looks almost new. Traveling would be so much easier if we had a boat as big as this, don't you think?
I'll be the captain, and Paimon, you can be the chief mate.
#Aye aye, Cap'n {NICKNAME}! Tying the jib to the mizzenmast and raising the port side anchor to the load line, Cap'n!
Hehe, how convincing is Paimon's chief mateyness? Come on, take the helm, and let's set sail!
Maybe it's a ship of dreams that ran aground before it ever set sail...
That must mean this is the Treasure Hoarders' secret dock! Hundreds of years have passed now, and the local geography's changed — Paimon figures it's probably never going to get the chance...

flow.stepDescription: Try taking the helm

dialogs.text: Bounty Island's just up ahead. Nothing about it looks particularly special from here.
Relya, I'm still not happy about this. I mean, the treasure here's been marked by the governor. If we take it...
Don't worry. We still have a few more days before the drill's over, and by the time the governor notices, we'll already be in Snezhnograd. No one'll think to come after us.
That's not what's bothering me... What if he ends up on the hook for telling us where the treasure is?
...Who? Oh, you mean that Brahe kid. What do you care? He's had his fair share of "the honey brewed for the few."
And I haven't?
What are you talking about? You and that kid are nothing alike. If you were on the same side as them, you wouldn't...
Ah! Don't worry about him, he'll be fine. He might be adopted, but he's still the governor's son. Besides, he's young — no one's gonna give him any trouble.
I hope you're right.
Ha! So this is what "Bounty Island" looks like. I guess it really does live up to its name.
What are we going to do with the loot? Same as usual? Though, if we're taking it back to Snezhnograd...
Why not give it to the kids on the streets? I ran into them a few days ago while out on patrol. That kid with the conch shell struck me as a smart one.
They'll know what to do with the treasure — and who best to share it with.
Suits me, let's do it your way.
But compared to the treasures on display in the governor's palace, these little trinkets are hardly even worth the bother...
Hmph... Even in a backwater like this, those arrogant fools still indulge in their outrageous extravagance... Their shiny facade can't hide the fact they're already rotten to the core.
Have you seen it yet? This place is no different from Snezhnograd.
Are we really supposed to fight to protect people like this? And protect them from those we have no quarrel with? The unseen, the downtrodden, the despised...
I understand your anger. But there's not much we can do.
There's not much we can do right now. But sooner or later, we have to upturn the status quo, to weed out the corruption root and stem. I must rise to the top — by any means necessary...
I count myself lucky to have ended up fighting by your side, Silve. But I often find myself looking back to where I came from...
It's a place my brothers and sisters remain — where they continue to endure hardships they should never have to bear. Tell me, those innocent souls — were they born to suffer like this?
If it's the law that is causing their suffering, then I shall rewrite the law. And if it's the corrupt nobles, then I shall purge them from their ranks!
One day, I'll raise an Elysium that belongs to us on this land — a land that has always belonged to us!
I believe in you, Relya. I know you can accomplish your dream.
...Let's not talk about that now. Even thieves have their code, so I'll leave this behind. That way, the governor will know who took his treasure.
It's just a pity I won't get to see his reaction myself.
Haha, that would be a sight to behold.

flow.stepDescription: Talk to Tolfin

dialogs.text: #Oh, if it isn't {NICKNAME} and Paimon! Have you two found the Great Treasure already?
If you mean that pile of old Iron Coins...
We left those Iron Coins exactly where we found them... Well, actually, they're on top now.
You tell Tolfin what happened at the treasure site and the strange things that happened after you boarded the ship...
For some reason, they left behind some sort of raven insignia.
It seems the earth remembers far more than we could ever imagine — as a storyteller, I can't help but feel humbled by that...
After all, human life is fleeting, and oral history is prone to errors — some stories may even be lost forever. Yet the earth's memory no doubt remains true.
I think it could only have been Avrelian who left that "raven insignia." You may be more familiar with another of his names — Reed Miller.
Huh!? You mean that was the legendary thief, Reed Miller? Paimon would never have guessed by looking at him...

From what you described, the things you saw almost certainly happened before the Treasure Hoarders were even formed. It's said that back then, he liked to play the role of heroic thief with his military academy buddies, stealing from the rich and helping the poor.
In fact, that raven insignia was derived from the family crest of his noble-born academy classmate.
But that's all in the past, so I shalln't bore you with the details. Anyway, seeing as our fates appear to be intertwined, how about you two take this raven insignia as a keepsake?
I assume accepting this doesn't automatically make me the Treasure Hoarders' heir...
Haha, there's no need to worry — like I said, the golden age of the Treasure Hoarders is over. However, there is still one slight problem...
My stubborn grandmother seems to have taken a liking to you. If she ever asks you for a friendly sparring match, please don't turn her down — and don't pull your punches, either.
Whoa, she's so much stronger than a regular old lady, we wouldn't dream of doing anything but pummeling her with everything we've got!
Well then, the Great Treasure buried "East of the Moon, West of the Sun" has been claimed by a pair of remarkable adventurers, and this performance, too, has come to its close.
Allow me to play you a tune, to express my wish that every step of your journey be filled with mystery, and every path may bring you jubilation.
Eh? Huh!? Wha!?! What just happened?
We found a Treasure Hoarder ship under a pile of Iron Coins, then you took the helm... After that, it felt like a dream, and then somehow, we ended up here...
Those two... they mentioned someone called "Brahe." Either it's a crazy coincidence, or they must be from a long, long time ago?
At the very least, we know they have a connection to this place.
Yeah! And from what they were saying, there was once some treasure buried here, and even though they made off with it, it seems they left something else in its place...?
It's been so long, who knows if someone's already dug it up by now...
Let's see if we can find it first.
Hmm, it can't hurt to look! If Paimon remembers correctly, it should be somewhere around... here!
Paimon can't believe it's still here! Why didn't the governor come to collect it?
Huh? This is what they left here? Isn't this...?
Hmm, Paimon doesn't understand. Let's ask Tolfin about it... Oh! Paimon almost forgot, we should tell him what happened with the Great Treasure, too!
